named.name: London Bridge
named.source: Old London Bridge, en.wikipedia.org (read 21 November 2026): of stone 1176-1209, 19 arches, houses on it from the start; Harrison 2004

named.name: Grand-Pont
named.source: Grand-Pont (Pont au Change), fr.wikipedia.org (read 21 November 2026): of stone under Louis VI, carried away by the flood of 1296; Boyer 1976

named.name: Petit-Pont
named.source: Petit-Pont, fr.wikipedia.org (read 21 November 2026): of stone under Louis VI, carried away by the flood of 1296; Boyer 1976

named.name: Pont Saint-Bénézet
named.source: Pont Saint-Bénézet, en.wikipedia.org (read 21 November 2026): stone arches, built 1177-1188; Boyer 1976

named.name: Ponte Vecchio
named.source: Ponte Vecchio, en.wikipedia.org (read 21 November 2026): rebuilt in stone after the flood of 1117, swept away 1333

named.name: Rialto Bridge
named.source: Rialto Bridge, en.wikipedia.org (read 21 November 2026): a timber bridge from 1255, of stone only from 1591

named.name: Judith Bridge
named.source: Judith Bridge, en.wikipedia.org (read 21 November 2026): of stone 1158-1172

named.name: Krämerbrücke
named.source: Liste mittelalterlicher Steinbrücken in Deutschland, de.wikipedia.org (read 21 November 2026): of stone only 1325; Krämerbrücke, de.wikipedia.org: of timber before

named.name: Steinerne Brücke
named.source: Liste mittelalterlicher Steinbrücken in Deutschland, de.wikipedia.org (read 21 November 2026): of stone 1135-1146, finished by 1147 at the latest

named.name: Alte Mainbrücke
named.source: Liste mittelalterlicher Steinbrücken in Deutschland, de.wikipedia.org (read 21 November 2026): of stone about 1120, destroyed 1342

named.name: Dammtorbrücke
named.source: Liste mittelalterlicher Steinbrücken in Deutschland, de.wikipedia.org (read 21 November 2026): of stone 1159 or soon after

named.name: Hohe Brücke
named.source: Liste mittelalterlicher Steinbrücken in Deutschland, de.wikipedia.org (read 21 November 2026): built of stone between 1172 and 1200

named.name: Steinbrücke
named.source: Liste mittelalterlicher Steinbrücken in Deutschland, de.wikipedia.org (read 21 November 2026): first named lapideus pons in 1229, 23 arches, 103 m

named.name: Pliensaubrücke
named.source: Liste mittelalterlicher Steinbrücken in Deutschland, de.wikipedia.org (read 21 November 2026): built about 1213-1259, first named 1286

named.name: Alte Brücke
named.source: Liste mittelalterlicher Steinbrücken in Deutschland, de.wikipedia.org (read 21 November 2026): first named as a stone bridge in 1276

ferry.name: Cologne
ferry.source: Die Geschichte der Kölner Rheinbrücken, stadt-koeln.de (read 21 November 2026): no fixed crossing of the Rhine for almost 900 years until the boat bridge of Deutz in 1822; in between only boats and ferry ships

ferry.name: Mainz
ferry.source: Historische Brücken, Blätter zum Land, Landeszentrale für politische Bildung Rheinland-Pfalz (read 21 November 2026): Charlemagne's timber bridge burnt in 813, the first fixed Rhine bridge again in 1862; travellers and goods were taken over by ferry

ferry.name: Seville
ferry.source: Triana (Seville), en.wikipedia.org (read 21 November 2026): a bridge of boats from 1171, destroyed by Ferdinand III in 1248; the first solid bridge in 1852 (Puente de Triana)

ferry.name: Bordeaux
ferry.source: Pont de pierre (Bordeaux), en.wikipedia.org (read 21 November 2026): the first bridge over the Garonne at Bordeaux, 1819-1822; until then the river was crossed by boat

ferry.name: Valence
ferry.source: Les deux ponts, Département de la Drôme (read 21 November 2026): fords, a supposed timber bridge and boatmen, joined in the Middle Ages by a cable ferry (bac à traille); the first bridge, of wire, in 1830

ferry.name: Pressburg
ferry.source: List of bridges in Bratislava city, en.wikipedia.org (read 21 November 2026): but for a short-lived bridge of the 15th century, the first bridge over the Danube was the pontoon bridge of Caroline Augusta of 1825

ferry.name: Buda
ferry.source: Buza, Péter (1999): Bridges of the Danube, Budapest, p. 8 (library.hungaricana.hu, read 21 November 2026): the boat-bridges of the Middle Ages lay at the foot of the Tabán valley; a fixed bridge between the twin towns only centuries later
